Draft — not yet reviewed

This policy is a working draft written from what the clinic’s own website says about its practice. The highlighted phrases are decisions only Halcyon can make, and the whole document should be checked by a lawyer against the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the medical records rules that apply in Telangana before it is published. Delete this box once it has been.

1. Who we are

Halcyon Pain Management Centre is a pain management clinic at 3rd Floor, KKR Commercial Complex, Kukatpally Y Junction, Moosapet Road, Hyderabad, Telangana 500072. In this policy, “we”, “us” and “Halcyon” mean that clinic, and “you” means anyone who contacts us, attends an appointment, or uses this website.

We decide how and why your personal data is handled, which under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 makes us the data fiduciary for it.

2. What this policy covers

It covers information you give us when you enquire, book, or attend the clinic, and anything this website collects. It does not cover other websites we link to — Google Maps for directions, for instance — which have their own policies.

3. What this website collects

Nothing.

As this site is built today, it sets no cookies, runs no analytics or tracking, and sends nothing you type anywhere. The assistant on the home page answers from a fixed list of answers held inside the page itself — your question is never transmitted to us or to anyone else, and nothing you type is stored once you close the tab.

Our web host may keep standard server logs of requests, including IP addresses, for security and troubleshooting. Confirm what your host logs and for how long.

If tracking, analytics, an online booking form or a live chat service are added later, this section must be rewritten before they go live, and a cookie notice may be required.

4. Information we collect

When you contact us

  • Your name and phone number when you call or message us.
  • Your email address if you write to us.
  • Anything you choose to send over WhatsApp, including scans, reports and photographs.

When you attend the clinic

  • Identification and contact details taken at reception.
  • Your medical history, symptoms and examination findings.
  • Diagnostic ultrasound images taken in the consulting room, and any X-ray, MRI, CT or other reports you bring or send.
  • Details of the procedures performed, medicines used, aftercare given and reviews attended.
  • Payment records. Confirm whether card details are held by the clinic or only by the payment provider.

Health information of this kind is sensitive. We ask for it only where it is needed to work out where your pain is coming from and to treat it safely.

5. Why we use it

  • To answer your enquiry and arrange an appointment.
  • To reach a diagnosis, plan treatment, and carry it out safely — including knowing about blood thinners, diabetes, blood pressure or pregnancy, which change what can be used.
  • To keep an accurate clinical record and to follow up after a procedure.
  • To raise and settle bills, and to support an insurance or reimbursement claim where you ask us to.
  • To meet our legal, professional and regulatory obligations as a medical establishment.

We do not sell your information, and we do not use it for advertising. Confirm whether appointment reminders or clinic updates are sent, and how people opt out.

6. Your consent

Where we rely on your consent, we ask for it before we take the information, and you may withdraw it at any time by contacting us. Withdrawing consent does not undo anything already done with the information, and there are records we must keep even after you withdraw — a clinical record of a procedure that has been performed, for example.

Some information we handle for reasons the law allows without separate consent, such as providing medical treatment in an emergency or complying with a legal requirement.

7. Who we share it with

We share your information only where there is a reason to, and only as much as is needed:

  • The consultants and clinical staff treating you.
  • Laboratories, imaging centres and other providers involved in your care. List the ones you use.
  • Your insurer or third-party administrator, where you ask us to support a claim.
  • A doctor who referred you, or one you ask us to write to.
  • Service providers who work on our behalf — for example the practice management or record-keeping software we use — under an obligation to keep it confidential. Name the systems that hold patient data.
  • Courts, regulators or public authorities where the law requires it.

Confirm whether any of these providers store data outside India.

8. How long we keep it

We keep clinical records for as long as we are required to, and for as long as they may be needed for your continuing care. Enquiries that do not lead to an appointment are kept for a shorter period and then deleted.

Set the actual retention periods here — for outpatient records, for images, for billing records, and for enquiries — against the medical records rules that apply to you.

9. How we protect it

Access to records is limited to the people who need it for your care or for running the clinic. Paper records are held securely at the clinic and electronic records are held on describe the systems and their protections — access control, encryption, backups.

If a breach happens that is likely to affect you, we will tell you and the Data Protection Board of India as the Act requires.

10. Your rights

Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you may:

  • Ask what personal data of yours we hold and what we have done with it.
  • Ask us to correct anything inaccurate, complete anything incomplete, or update anything that has changed.
  • Ask us to erase your personal data, where we are not required to keep it.
  • Withdraw a consent you have given.
  • Nominate someone to exercise these rights on your behalf if you are unable to.
  • Raise a grievance with us, and escalate to the Data Protection Board of India if you are not satisfied with how we answer.

Write to info@halcyonpainfree.com or call +91 77880 91092, and we will respond within state your response time. We may need to confirm who you are before we act on a request.

11. Children

Where a patient is under 18, we take the information from a parent or guardian and act on their consent. This website is not directed at children and does not knowingly collect anything from them.

12. Changes to this policy

If our practices change — particularly if this website starts collecting anything — we will update this page and change the date at the top. Material changes will be brought to your attention rather than left to be discovered.

13. Contact and grievances

For anything in this policy, or to exercise a right under it, contact name and email of the person handling data protection grievances — or use the clinic’s general contacts below. The Act requires a grievance to be answered before it can be escalated to the Data Protection Board of India.

Ask us anything about your records.

If you want to know what we hold, have something corrected, or would rather we deleted an enquiry, the same numbers that book appointments will reach the team.
